plugins/transforms/aws/textract_document: `isinstance(identity, TextractProfiledAuditIdentity)` is the nominal admission check on the Web-only audit authority that `web/execution/preflight.py` binds after runtime construction. The parameter is deliberately typed `object` because a typed signature is not a runtime control: this method is the only place the transform accepts an identity that later drives `_audit_location_identity` and the HMAC binding-fingerprint comparison below it, so an impostor must be refused here, and a raise on anything but the concrete owned frozen class is ADR-032 rule 1 (nominally type what ELSPETH owns; never a runtime_checkable Protocol). Nothing is defaulted or coerced — the check exists so that no forgeable config field can stand in for the identity.

`isinstance(location, TransformResult)` is nominal discrimination against `TransformResult`, a concrete class ELSPETH owns, over the Tier-2 union `_read_document_location` returns (`tuple[str, str, str | None] | TransformResult`): the early-return arm carries an already-built row error result (missing/invalid bucket, key or version), the other arm carries the validated S3 location that is then unpacked. This is ADR-032 rule 1 (internal boundary: isinstance against an owned concrete class), not a Tier-3 shape guard, and neither arm defaults or coerces — the same shape B20 rationalised in textract_inline_analysis._process_single_with_state.

`isinstance(collected, TransformResult)` discriminates the Tier-2 union `_poll_and_collect` returns (`tuple[Mapping[str, Any], ...] | TransformResult`): a routed row error (poll_timeout, shutdown_requested, malformed_response, too_many_blocks, pagination_cycle …) versus the collected SUCCEEDED pages that `normalize_textract_result` then validates. `TransformResult` is a concrete owned class, so this is ADR-032 rule 1 nominal typing of an internal seam; the error arm is returned unchanged and the page arm is fully re-validated downstream, so nothing is defaulted.
plugins/transforms/field_mapper.py:R6:_n: `except ExternalHeaderError: return False` is the predicate's documented negative answer, not a swallow: `_names_a_row_key` asks whether a config literal is a fixed point of `normalize_field_name`, and a literal that normalizes to NOTHING (the only case that raises `ExternalHeaderError`) names no row field at all because the source boundary rejects such a header, so `False` is the correct and only truthful value. The handler is narrowed to the one owned exception class that means exactly that; a bare `ValueError` from an algorithm bug still propagates, so the error class a bad mapping key raises at construction is unchanged. This mirrors `value_transform._row_key_aliases` deliberately, and returning `False` here is what lets `declared_input_fields` ABSTAIN rather than assert a row key that cannot exist (elspeth-f262a8c678).
